status_summary: The Space Force released a planning framework on 2025-04-17 that describes offensive counterspace options (orbital strike, space link interdiction and terrestrial strike) alongside defensive ones. EO 14369 (signed 2025-12-18) directs the government to be able to detect, characterize and counter threats to U.S. space interests from very low Earth orbit through cislunar space and does not mention offensive capabilities, space control or the Space Force. CRS puts the FY2027 Space Force request at about 71.3 billion dollars, including 12.1 billion in anticipated mandatory funding, against 31.9 billion enacted for FY2026, with 2,800 more military personnel, and a trade report puts space control at 21.6 billion; the request is not enacted. EO 14423 (signed 2026-08-28) created a NASA-chaired commission to advise within 120 days on a proposed NASA-led U.S. Space Academy, and no source was found on added general officer positions, declassification, or a Space Force academy.

timeline.event: Space Force releases the Space Warfighting framework describing orbital, link and terrestrial offensive counterspace options.
EO 14369 signed: ability to detect, characterize and counter threats from very low Earth orbit through cislunar space; it does not mention offensive capabilities or the Space Force.
Chief of Space Operations testifies to the House Armed Services Committee on a FY2027 Space Force request reported at 71.1 billion dollars, including 21.6 billion for space control.
EO 14423 signed, creating a commission chaired by the NASA Administrator to advise on a proposed NASA-led United States Space Academy and report within 120 days.

title: Space Force: restore offensive options, expand space control, reduce secrecy, add generals
uncertainties: The framework document itself and the testimony were not read; DefenseScoop and a secondary summary were used, and the FY2027 total appears as 71.1 billion in the testimony summary and 71.3 billion in CRS. TWZ reports a FY2026 Space Force figure of about 40 billion, which differs from the 31.9 billion CRS gives for FY2026 enacted. Existing offensive systems are classified and not assessed. CRS says the commission will consider a NASA framework among others and does not describe a Space Force academy; the Secretary of the Air Force is a commission member. No source on general officer numbers was found. Golden Dome is covered in c04-07 and is not restated.
